Confirmed: 'metformin hcl er 1' and 'metformin hcl oral tablet 1000 mg, 500 mg, 850 mg 1' (page 31, Tier 1, no restriction symbol). Confirmed 'metformin hcl er (mod) E PA' and 'metformin hcl er (osm) E PA' (page 31) and 'metformin hcl oral tablet 625 mg, 750 mg E' (page 31) -- all marked with PA/exclusion flags. 'GLUMETZA ORAL TABLET EXTENDED RELEASE 24 HOUR 1000 MG, 500 MG E PA' (page 31) confirms the brand ER product also requires PA. Alternatives (glipizide XL, glimepiride, pioglitazone) confirmed Tier 1 on page 30-31 as other first-line-adjacent oral options in the same Non-Insulin Agents section. Sig (500mg BID with meals, titrate) is standard metformin FDA-label dosing, not stated verbatim in the PDL, which lists coverage/tier only. records.verificationNote: Read directly from the UnitedHealthcare 2026 PDL, effective January 1, 2026, pages 30-31 (Diabetes - Non-Insulin Agents). Confirmed: 'OZEMPIC 2 PA, QL' (page 31), 'TRULICITY 2 PA, QL' (page 31), 'MOUNJARO 2 PA, QL' (page 31), 'RYBELSUS 2 PA, QL' (page 31), 'liraglutide solution pen-injector 18 mg/3ml subcutaneous 2 PA, QL (2-pack)' and '...3 PA, QL (3-pack)' (page 31), 'BYDUREON BCISE AUTOINJECTOR SUBCUTANEOUS AUTO-INJECTOR 2 MG/0.85ML 2 PA, QL' (page 30), 'SOLIQUA 2 QL' (page 31). Every GLP-1 agent on this PDL requires PA regardless of tier -- this is a class-wide pattern, not specific to non-preferred agents, so Ozempic was selected as the preferred/most commonly first-line agent per current ADA/clinical guidance, all sitting at the same Tier 2 with the same PA+QL restriction profile. No agent in this class is PA-free on this PDL. Sig reflects standard Ozempic FDA-label dose-titration schedule, not stated verbatim in the PDL. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.tier: Tier 1 (lowest member cost) for LANTUS SOLOSTAR/vial and HUMALOG VIAL/MIX vials
records.verificationNote: Read directly from the UnitedHealthcare 2026 PDL, effective January 1, 2026, pages 29-30 (Diabetes - Insulin). Confirmed: 'LANTUS SOLOSTAR 1 QL' and 'LANTUS U-100 VIAL 1 QL' (page 30) vs. 'INSULIN GLARGINE E QL', 'INSULIN GLARGINE MAX SOLOSTAR E QL', 'INSULIN GLARGINE SOLOSTAR E QL' (page 30) -- brand clean-covered, generic/authorized-generic PA-flagged. Confirmed 'HUMALOG MIX 50/50 VIAL...1 QL', 'HUMALOG MIX 75/25 VIAL 1 QL', 'HUMULIN N VIAL 1 QL', 'HUMULIN R VIAL 1 QL' (pages 29-30) at Tier 1. Confirmed 'INSULIN ASPART E ST, QL', 'INSULIN ASPART FLEXPEN E ST, QL' (page 30) and the full NOVOLIN/NOVOLOG family all marked 'E ST, QL' (page 30) -- explicit step-therapy symbol. Confirmed 'TRESIBA FLEXTOUCH E QL', 'INSULIN DEGLUDEC FLEXTOUCH E QL', 'BASAGLAR TEMPO PEN E QL', 'ADMELOG E QL', 'ADMELOG SOLOSTAR E QL', 'HUMALOG TEMPO PEN E QL' (pages 29-30) -- all PA/exclusion-flagged. TOUJEO and LYUMJEV confirmed Tier 1-2 with QL only, no PA/ST symbol (page 30). This class shows the most brand-over-generic (BOGL) activity of the ten classes reviewed: multiple brand insulins (Lantus, Humalog) are cleanly covered while their own authorized generics or class competitors carry PA/ST flags. Sig reflects standard basal-insulin dosing convention, not stated verbatim in the PDL. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]
